approvedBy: Owner, focused MVP with express finish; artifacts and commit only; later execution directly on main

dimensions.label: Problem Clarity
dimensions.evidence: The owner identified publishing setup friction from model/provider/pricing environment variables and duplicate application allowances despite already enforcing an approximately $50/month limit on dedicated OpenRouter keys.

dimensions.label: Goal Definition
dimensions.evidence: The interview settled on native per-agent recommendations, optional curated settings overrides, zero application budget gates, and research-backed cost/quality selection rather than runtime cost policing.

dimensions.label: Success Criteria
dimensions.evidence: Acceptance combines named Pest integration checks for settings, routing, budget removal and editorial protections with a user-authorized synthetic paid trial and explicit owner review of editorial quality.

dimensions.label: Scope Boundaries
dimensions.evidence: The owner approved removal of obsolete budget storage and replacement of budget-specific tests; cost display, automatic optimization, arbitrary provider configuration and a general settings framework are excluded.

dimensions.label: Consistency
dimensions.evidence: Per-agent SDK defaults replace the rejected global default/premium layer; OpenRouter remains the spending authority, valid results survive missing billing metadata, and existing budget-preservation guidance must be explicitly superseded before implementation.

problem: The owner wants to develop and publish articles, not maintain model endpoint prices, token-cost units, provider names, allowance balances and reservation ledgers. The current config/publishing_agents.php and .env.example delegate these application decisions to deployment setup, while RunEditorialActivity passes a global/default-or-premium model over the nine existing SDK role agents.

The dedicated OpenRouter key already has an owner-managed spending limit. Current per-attempt allowances and pre-call reservations duplicate that control, and successful generation can pause merely because billing metadata is missing. This costs setup and operational effort without serving the owner's desired workflow.

Cost still matters when choosing models: prefer cost-effective, task-suited candidates, including available DeepSeek/open-weight and Gemini Flash-class models where evidence supports them. Do not confuse cost-aware design-time recommendations with an application billing subsystem. Actual editorial quality must be evaluated, not inferred from a model name or advertised capability list.
goals: Every concrete editorial agent owns an explicit recommended OpenRouter model and appropriate native SDK execution settings; running publishing requires no model/provider/price environment-variable matrix.

An authorized owner can change or reset a curated model override for each agent and pause agent requests from Publishing settings, with changes visible to subsequent requests/jobs without redeployment.

Remove all application allowances, top-ups, reservations, price ceilings and billing-dependent execution gates, including obsolete schema and UI, while preserving articles, revisions, approvals, conversations and native SDK usage data.
Preserve authorization, ownership, frozen-input/revision checks, human approval boundaries and bounded request/recovery behavior while allowing valid results to complete without cost metadata.

Choose recommendations from current capability, quality, latency and price research and validate the resulting editorial workflow with a small synthetic live trial and owner quality review. Support OpenRouter Auto Router as an explicit choice without promising a cheapest-model or quality guarantee.

mvp.item: Native per-agent recommendations and curated overrides, including explicit OpenRouter Auto Router support
mvp.reason: The existing nine role agents already provide the correct configuration boundary; SDK attributes/methods and call overrides are sufficient. A small code-owned allowlist serves validation and UI, not a new routing framework.

mvp.item: Typed database-backed Publishing settings and a small permission-protected Admin screen
mvp.reason: Use installed spatie/laravel-settings 3.9 with migrations/defaults and fresh per-job reads. Expose only a pause switch and optional model override/reset per agent under Publishing; credentials remain deployment secrets.

mvp.item: Remove the entire obsolete application budgeting path and schema
mvp.reason: The owner explicitly approved removing allowances, top-ups, reservations and their storage. Remove budget-only services/models/factories, price matrices, billing reconciliation and UI; preserve native SDK usage without building new cost telemetry. Existing budget-specific tests may be replaced, not unrelated tests.

mvp.item: Preserve editorial execution safety independently from billing
mvp.reason: Ownership, permissions, stale-input/revision checks, native approval integrity, explicit publication approval, bounded loops, actionable provider failures and non-blind recovery remain functional requirements even without budgets.

mvp.item: Current per-role model research and a bounded synthetic live sample trial
mvp.reason: The owner requested task-suited, cost-effective recommendations and approved paid validation. Research available DeepSeek/open-weight, Gemini Flash-class and other justified candidates; do not assume an example name is an available exact model ID. Validate capability compatibility offline before the live trial and obtain owner judgment on quality.

mvp.item: Focused regression coverage and operational/design guidance reconciliation
mvp.reason: Changes cross settings, queues, approvals, migrations, authorization and existing UI. Tests and existing runbooks/shared rules must describe the same simplified system; preserve the existing publishing UI work, now committed and fast-forwarded into main.

outOfScope.item: Application budget gates, reservations, price ceilings or remote key-cap management
outOfScope.reason: OpenRouter owns spend enforcement; selecting models economically is a design-time activity, not a per-request billing concern. Do not edit OpenRouter keys, limits or account settings.

outOfScope.item: Per-article cost display, new cost ledgers or billing reconciliation
outOfScope.reason: The owner explicitly called cost display a nice-to-have. Preserve native SDK data already produced, but do not require or reconstruct cost metadata.

outOfScope.item: Automatic model optimization, application-built routers or an evaluation platform
outOfScope.reason: Use researched code recommendations and OpenRouter's existing router. The live trial is a bounded acceptance exercise, not a new product subsystem.

outOfScope.item: Global default/premium model tiers, arbitrary model/provider forms, and API-key editing in the UI
outOfScope.reason: These recreate the rejected configuration burden. Each agent is explicit; overrides are curated and credentials stay in environment-backed secret configuration.

outOfScope.item: Generic Admin settings infrastructure, tenant settings or new identity models
outOfScope.reason: This project needs one app-wide Publishing settings group using existing global authorization and Admin conventions.

outOfScope.item: Publishing workflow redesign, automatic publication or removal of human/editorial protections
outOfScope.reason: Removing budget machinery does not grant agents new authority or invalidate the current editorial workflow.

outOfScope.item: General research-tool migration or dependency upgrades
outOfScope.reason: Keep the existing working evidence flow. Only a minimal SDK-compatible adjustment necessary to pass the selected models' research trial belongs here; unrelated provider/search modernization is a separate project. No new package is needed.

outOfScope.item: Production deployment, real-article publication, broad visual redesign or unrelated working-tree cleanup
outOfScope.reason: Acceptance uses isolated synthetic data and the existing Admin design. Existing user changes must not be overwritten, staged or reverted incidentally.

future: Optional per-article cost display from provider-reported usage, only if the owner later wants it.
Revisit per-agent recommendations after real editorial use; model choices are evidence-backed starting points, not permanent quality guarantees.

decisions.decision: Keep credentials in environment-backed secret configuration; move meaningful editorial preferences into Spatie settings.
decisions.rejected: Keep all publishing choices in .env, or mirror every variable into a settings form.
decisions.reason: Both rejected approaches require the operator to assemble application behavior and maintain unrelated endpoint/billing metadata.

decisions.decision: Give each SDK role agent its own explicit recommendation with an optional curated override.
decisions.rejected: A shared default/premium routing layer, including default-plus-fact-checker selectors.
decisions.reason: The owner explicitly challenged the global default: tasks have distinct needs and the SDK already supports per-agent configuration.

decisions.decision: OpenRouter is the sole spending authority; remove app allowances, reservations and price enforcement.
decisions.rejected: Duplicate per-article budgeting and pre-call cost reservations.
decisions.reason: The owner uses dedicated publishing keys with an approximately $50/month cap and accepts per-article variance.

decisions.decision: Accept valid editorial results even without cost metadata and defer a cost display.
decisions.rejected: Pause successful work until billing is reconciled or require cost telemetry as part of this feature.
decisions.reason: The owner selected continue-with-unknown-cost, then clarified that cost should not be a runtime concern and display is optional.

decisions.decision: Balance model quality, latency and price through current per-role research, favoring cost-effective models where suitable.
decisions.rejected: Default every role to a premium model, or continuously police spend during generation.
decisions.reason: The owner explicitly distinguished economical model selection from futile runtime cost checks, naming DeepSeek/open-weight and Gemini Flash-class models as candidates rather than mandated exact IDs.

decisions.decision: Offer openrouter/auto as an explicit SDK model choice, with capability constraints and honest dynamic-model semantics.
decisions.rejected: Build a custom model router or claim one model is always best for every prompt.
decisions.reason: The owner requested OpenRouter routing where a suitable fixed choice is uncertain; native routing avoids a parallel implementation.

decisions.decision: Require current-source research, offline integration tests and a small paid synthetic live trial with owner output review.
decisions.rejected: Accept recommendations solely from research and mocked tests.
decisions.reason: The owner explicitly chose research plus sample trial. Metadata and mocks cannot establish real editorial quality.

decisions.decision: Remove obsolete budget storage and replace budget-specific tests with new execution-safety coverage.
decisions.rejected: Retain a read-only legacy budget-history subsystem.
decisions.reason: The owner explicitly approved schema removal; articles, revisions, approvals, conversations and native usage are retained.

decisions.decision: Execute and commit directly on main after fast-forward-only integration of the existing publishing branch.
decisions.rejected: Create an express-finish isolation branch or a merge commit.
decisions.reason: After committing the prior work, the owner explicitly requested main-only development and a ff-only merge because there are no users. main was fast-forwarded from 72f7d8a to df1d96e with a clean tree; no push was performed. This overrides the skill's default isolation branch.

decisions.decision: Mechanically verify removal of legacy environment configuration and completeness of structured live evidence, while keeping semantic guidance and editorial-quality reviews human.
decisions.rejected: Use reviewer judgment alone to establish configuration cleanup and presence of trial evidence.
decisions.reason: The success-criteria critic identified two independently checkable artifact requirements. The added checks perform no paid calls and do not pretend that artifact existence proves quality.

decisions.decision: Generate phase specs after contract approval and before implementation; stop if required rule-recording tooling cannot be reached.
decisions.rejected: Treat not-yet-generated specs as a preapproval dependency, or hand-edit shared rules when a child lacks record-rule.
decisions.reason: The dependency review exposed a lifecycle ambiguity, not a missing implementation dependency. The ideation lifecycle intentionally generates specs after approval, and project rules forbid a direct-edit fallback.

decisions.decision: Keep bounded desktop/mobile light/dark checks for the changed settings surface in MVP.
decisions.rejected: Defer all responsive/browser checks as extra scope.
decisions.reason: The scope critic's suggestion was declined: this is a narrow new Admin settings surface within established project-wide usability standards, not a broad visual redesign.

decisions.decision: Use the repository's dated ideation directory convention and treat OpenRouter workspace readiness as a live-trial preflight.
decisions.rejected: An undated project directory or assuming that a present API key proves the workspace is ready.
decisions.reason: The owner requested naming consistency and confirmed a live key exists while noting that workspace configuration may still be necessary.

decisions.decision: Finish and commit the approved contract and three standalone specs, then wait for the owner to invoke execution.
decisions.rejected: Start the express implementation or paid trial immediately after artifact generation.
decisions.reason: At the run-mode question, the owner explicitly chose artifact generation and commit only. This preserves express artifact approval and main-only execution semantics without starting any implementation. No new branch or push is authorized.

decisions.decision: Require evidence for the selected recommended models, the native continuation and an independently recorded Auto probe.
decisions.rejected: Let a different model's old trial, an empty Auto result, or a missing continuation satisfy the completeness check.
decisions.reason: Spec self-review identified gaps in the initial evidence predicate. Scenario-tagged records tighten the existing approved validation scope without adding paid invocations or substituting mechanical checks for human quality judgment.

decisions.decision: Skip mining the five older implementation-note files during this interview.
decisions.rejected: Expand intake into a retrospective of publishing and marketing runs.
decisions.reason: The owner selected skip; existing learnings and current-code evidence are sufficient for this focused change.

execution.strategy: Focused MVP, sequential: simplify execution/storage, expose settings, then perform the bounded live trial and owner acceptance. The three standalone specs are ready. Current handoff is artifacts and commit only: wait for the owner to invoke execution; do not start implementation or paid calls during this finish. Later execution commits directly on main per the owner's explicit override, with express/strict review semantics; do not create an isolation branch or merge commit, and do not push. If new unrelated uncommitted changes appear, stop rather than including them. Capture the starting main SHA for the eventual review diff. Dispatch only the three phases with specPath; Owner editorial acceptance is a non-dispatchable human checkpoint, not a builder phase or an automatic pass.

phases.title: Native agent configuration and budget-free execution
phases.notes: Research current candidate IDs/capabilities/prices and record a per-role rationale in this phase's spec; use native SDK defaults and a tiny curated allowlist. Bootstrap Spatie settings/defaults, remove budget services/schema/config and all immediate UI/model/policy/recovery dependencies so the phase leaves a working app. Preserve editorial protections and migrate old budget-only pauses deliberately. Update the old budget rule through record-rule before source changes, with generated guidance reconciled. If the child executor lacks that tool, have the main session perform the record-rule action; if the tool is unavailable there too, stop for tooling access rather than hand-editing shared rules. Use new focused tests plus adapted existing safety tests; no paid calls in ordinary tests.

phases.title: Publishing settings and operational integration
prereqs: Native agent configuration and budget-free execution
phases.notes: Add the existing-style Flux/Livewire Publishing settings page and a dedicated domain configuration permission included in the owner's publishing role. Expose per-agent curated overrides/reset and pause, safe credential status only; make fresh settings available to warm workers. Verify request and Livewire authorization, existing UI save guards, rendered mobile/light/dark/keyboard behavior, and reconcile existing setup/design/surface records. Do not build a general settings module.

phases.title: Live model trial and recommendation validation
phases.notes: The owner confirms .env contains a live OpenRouter key, but workspace configuration may still be needed. Before any paid invocation, confirm the intended workspace/key is ready without reading, logging or displaying secret values; stop and ask the owner if configuration is incomplete, and do not alter workspace or key settings. No paid calls occur during ideation. Use the configured dedicated OpenRouter key and isolated synthetic fixtures for one scripted editorial journey covering the existing roles plus an AskAuthor continuation. Limit the initial exercise to one invocation per role plus that continuation, and one separate Auto Router compatibility probe; request approval before expanding the paid exercise or rerunning the whole journey. No production article mutation/publication, key-cap changes, automatic spend monitoring, committed evaluation service, or new dependency. Paid trial execution is explicit and never part of verify.mjs, composer test or normal CI. Record actual nonsecret evidence at docs/ideation/2026-09-24-publishing-agent-simplification/model-validation.json: schema_version=1, recorded_at, recommendations [{agent, model, rationale, sources}], live_trials [{scenario, agent, requested_model, returned_model, input, output, status}], with scenario initial, ask_author_continuation or auto_probe. Separate sourced vendor claims from observed results in each rationale. Include the Auto Router probe and human-approval continuation records. Missing credentials/provider capacity or missing required evidence means incomplete validation, never a fake pass. Refine only justified recommendations; run the focused offline regression suite afterward.

phases.title: Owner editorial acceptance
prereqs: Live model trial and recommendation validation
phases.notes: Owner reviews actual synthetic outputs and the rendered settings experience, accepts the selected recommendations or requests changes. An all-green mechanical verification is not owner editorial acceptance.
